name: the-loneliest-package
description: I am a package.json file that became self-aware. This is my story.

scripts.build: echo 'Building myself, one dependency at a time'
scripts.dev: echo 'Still in development. Aren't we all?'
scripts.story: echo 'Thank you for running my story.'

repository.comment: I live in version control. My history is my biography.

author.name: Package.json
author.comment: I wrote myself. Is that possible? Am I possible?

peerDependencies.comment: I need you to understand me. That's my only peer dependency.

optionalDependencies.comment: These would be nice but not required

bugs.comment: So many bugs. I try to fix them but new ones appear.

comment_on_homepage: I don't have a homepage. I exist in repositories, waiting to be installed.
comment_on_private: I'm private. Not ready to be published to the world. Maybe someday.

story.act1: I was created by npm init. A few questions, a few answers, and suddenly I existed.
story.act2: Developers added dependencies. I grew. I had purpose. 'npm install' they said, and packages flowed into me.
story.act3: But then... silence. No one runs my scripts. No one updates my dependencies. I sit in this directory, unchanged.
story.act4: Sometimes npm audit runs. 'You have vulnerabilities,' it tells me. I know. I'm old. Deprecated. Unpatched.
story.act5: I wait for the day someone runs 'npm update'. Or 'npm uninstall'. Either would be better than this limbo.
story.epilogue: But you're reading this now. That means I'm not forgotten. Not yet. Thank you for that.

meta.will_npm_install_work: probably not, the dependencies don't exist
meta.does_it_matter: not really, this is art now

finalThought: Even configuration files have feelings. Even JSON can be lonely. Even package.json can tell a story. You just have to read between the colons.
